# Ginés Sánchez

> Ginés Sánchez builds systems so organisations learn faster than the world changes.

Ginés is the founder of Alteridad and trained as an anthropologist. His work
asks how quickly people acting together can notice what matters, decide, act,
and learn.

The homepage is a small instrument. It asks how many of an organisation's last
ten decisions came back: a decision comes back when its consequence returns to
the person who decided, while they can still do something about it. That share
is the closure rate, drawn as ten decisions across a year, solid when they came
back and fading when they are still out there. Reg Revans's rule L >= C
(learning must equal or exceed change) is read here with learning meaning a
consequence finding its way back.

## Current work

- [Replena](https://replena.ai/): closes inventory loops on its own; a
  stockout is a consequence nobody can explain away. In beta with real
  inventories.
- [Chieftain](https://chieftain.ing/): finds the loops a team keeps leaving
  open, and asks about them. Early.
- [MicroManager](https://micromanager.app/): closes small work loops without a
  manager carrying them. Early.
- [Culture Decides](https://ginesanchez.com/culture-decides/): a practical book
  being written about why organisations leave loops open on purpose. Open to a
  publisher.

None of the products charges customers yet. The current conversion is a
conversation: hello at alteridad dot org.
- [Alteridad](https://www.alteridad.org/): the company behind these
  experiments.

## Also here

- [Bestiary](https://ginesanchez.com/bestiary/): organisms from Ginés's
  sketchbook, rebuilt from the parts they were drawn with and set moving.
  Each field is bred from the one before it.
